utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the order reflecting the fact that General Ratko Mladic presided over the hand-over of duties between the former corps commander, General Zivanovic, and General Milorad Krstic, who is now assuming full command of the Drina Corps at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next document, still on 13 July, 65 ter 77.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is another -- this is one of those State Security reports from Dragan Kijac, and I just want to ask you about one part of it, where it says, "Ibgan Mustafic, a former..." This is the first paragraph, at the bottom of the first paragraph: "Mustafic, a former SDA deputy in the former BH Assembly and a great opponent of Naser Oric, was among the prisoners and can, with necessary preparation, be used well in the media." Does this Mustafic person come up in the -- in your analysis? Is he identified by other material or personnel?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some notations, not necessarily documents; but through the course of the investigation, it was confirmed that this particular individual was, in fact, an opponent of Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was there any evidence from any source that he was, in fact, captured?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe, as the course of the investigation, he was captured, he was not executed, and he survived the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Any indication where he was identified on 13 July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next document, 65 ter 116.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is from now Commander Krstic, an order to the Bratunac and Milici and Skelani units. Can you, again, briefly tell us what Krstic is doing here or how it relates to location of those Bratunac Brigade forces that you have been talking about in that sweeping operation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In conjunction with the upcoming Srebrenica -- I'm sorry, upcoming Zepa operation, you know, General Krstic is also directing the units that had perimeters around the enclaves, specifically the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, the Skelani Separate Battalion, and the Milici Light Infantry Brigade, to conduct various sweep operations to continue going through the entire enclave, in part to ensure individuals from the enclave did not make their way to Zepa. Particularly in the case of the Bratunac Brigade, these trig points and these locations will line up to subsequent orders that are issued to the Bratunac Brigade commander, essentially, you know, a reflection of the Bratunac Brigade commander following these instructions and issuing more detailed orders to his subordinate battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter 131.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And it's a one-page document. In the English it translates both the typed version and a handwritten version; and then there's a two-page document in the B/C/S, the first being typed and the second being a handwritten version. This is from the Command of the Rogatica Brigade, as we know, the Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, 13 July, from Tolimir. What do you -- and it's to General Gvero personally, and it's entitled: "Accommodation of prisoners of war," and we can read what it says. How does this fit into your analysis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I don't know whether Mr. McCloskey minds dealing with what we regard the important translation issue on this document, the unknown word in the second line of the first paragraph. The word in B/C/S is "palacana," and Mr. McCloskey might recall that it's been dealt with previously, if he could help. If he can't, we say it means something along the lines of "sleeping place."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I remember now. Yeah, that -- I'll go with their definition on that --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you both.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But I don't know if anyone else recalls that, it was a long time ago, but I do and I don't see a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we can perhaps help, Mr. Butler, their version of the translation of part of this is "a sleeping place." Is that in replace of "accommodation"? Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could work interchangeably, for the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how does this fit into your analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the first level, it's a reflection that at this point in time, that General Tolimir is aware of the large quantity of prisoners that are being taken with respect -- with respect to Srebrenica, and that there are outstanding problems with finding adequate space for all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when he -- is this a document -- had you referred to this brief before in your testimony? When I'd asked you about Tolimir, was there something later on that you became aware of?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I thought you were referring to prior court appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're starting to string along.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You've just testified about something that sounds very similar to this.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you connect that for us?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is what I was referring to with respect to the earlier order by Tolimir, where he was -- it appeared that he had no information yet with respect to the fact that prisoners were being executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, that last line says: "It would be best if this new group which has not been in contact with the other prisoners of war." Do you know what he's talking about, "new group" and "other prisoners of war"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a practical matter, if you're well -- if you're able to segregate prisoners who have no awareness yet that their counterparts are being killed, it would make them a lot easier to guard at that location to the south. If prisoners are aware, you know, through their own observations or they've heard through the grapevine, so to speak that, you know, that ultimately they're going to be killed, they have a far higher incentive to want to escape and become security problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you -- what can you conclude, if anything, about the presence of General Gvero, the location of General Gvero, from this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I conclude from this document that General Gvero is present at the Main Staff headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go on to 65 ter 113.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is from IKM of the Drina Corps, 13 July, Main Staff Intelligence Sector, to the Command of the Drina Corps Intelligence Department, under the name of Colonel Radoslav Jankovic, and this is a report that we can see on the situation of the evacuation, UNPROFOR, other things that I don't want to get in with you. But where do you believe Colonel Radoslav Jankovic is at the time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe Colonel Radoslav Jankovic is at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And have you had a chance to look at the original documents related to this communication?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we'll be getting to a communication in the name of Momir Nikolic on I believe it's the 18th of July. Were you able to relate that at all with this document? And we'll talk in more detail about it when we get to the 18th.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, in the sense that the handwritten draft versions of this document and the document on the 18th appear to be written by the same person. In fact, in the document on the 18th, it has the initials "RJ."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So which person are you saying --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we get -- yeah, when we get to that document, it would have been Radoslav Jankovic also as the author, even though it is, in the typed version of the document, it's noted the author is Captain First Class Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll -- we'll get to that a bit -- a bit later. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now let's go to 65 ter 3013.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is -- now we're into 14 July. This is Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. It says, "Open text," from Commander Ratko Mladic, and it's a reference to enabling the honourable send-off of a group of 50 members of the Dutch Battalion from Bratunac to Ljubovija. What is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in relation to the members of the UN Dutch Battalion who are being detained at the Hotel Fontana.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know where these Dutch Battalion guys actually went?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They in fact did cross the bridge and go over to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And in paragraph 3, and the English, have you been able to make out that name?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could blow up paragraph 3 in the -- in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, in the English translation, it's listed as "Colonel Savo Bosanovic" However, when you go to paragraph 3 of the teleprinter version, the B/C/S version, and you look particularly closely, you can see a teleprinter double strike where it is, in fact, an "S" on top of a "K." So, in fact, the individual they're referring to is Colonel Savo Sikanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And remind us who that is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is an officer on the Main Staff, Morale, Legal, and Religious Affairs sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you see another version of this document that actually had his name spelled out correctly?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. When I first noticed this a number of days ago, the Evidence Section managed to find another version of this exact document, where, in fact, the teleprinter operated correctly and the name is spelled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter 1154A, and B in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is an intercept from 14 July at 0805 hours, between General Mladic and an unidentified male person. Now, just very simply, does this help you identify anything about the plans of General Mladic; I mean, where he's going to be?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- towards the very end of the intercept, it reflects the fact that until 1500 hours, "and then I'm going to the field. I'll be busy for two or three days and then I'm coming back." In reality, unbeknownst to President Karadzic and the political leadership of the RS at the time, General Mladic was going to Belgrade, where he would be meeting with members of the International Community, as well as with President Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And this reference to, "and where's Pepo?" "Pepo is in the field." Do you have any information on who Pepo is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, with respect to prior in evidence from either in this trial or in the past one with Colonel Borovcanin -- I'm sorry, Colonel Blagojevic, "Pepo" is the nickname that Colonel Salapura from the Main Staff attributes to himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And remind us, Salapura, what branch was he part of?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Salapura was with the Main Staff intelligence and security sector. He was the chief of intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's now go to tab 39, skipping ahead, 65 ter 89.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's 14 July still, where another one of these reports from Dragan Kijac, and I -- you can -- I mean, we can all read that first paragraph. That's not what I'm really interested in. We see, in the -- do you see that document? Do you have that one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. After providing that information, Kijac says: "We would like to mention that said reports were submitted to the Zvornik SJB, PJP, and deputy commander of the RS Special Brigade in the field." So who would that be that's the deputy commander of the RS MUP Special Brigade in the field on 14 July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be Mr. Borovcanin, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go on to 65 ter 183.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is a communication where we see a time of about 1745 hours up in the right-hand corner, and it's again from the Rogatica Brigade, from General Tolimir, and it's to the Main Staff, personally to General Miletic, entitled: "Protection of TVP." Now, we can read this to ourselves, but what is General Tolimir doing here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What General Tolimir is doing is requesting certain radio and encryption equipment to allow him to more completely monitor the radio activities of the brigades and tactical units that are involved in military activities around Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what significance, if any, is the fact that it's to -- personally to General Miletic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't attribute any particular significance to it. This is, in fact, who it should be addressed to. General Miletic, since communications falls under the operative -- or operations purview, would be the person who General Tolimir would want to handle this or to delegate officers on his staff to handle this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's -- let's skip ahead, Mr. Butler, to your tab 45.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 2670 -- In fact, let's skip that and get to 15 July, to tab 46, 65 ter 254.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is a daily combat report from the Command of the Bratunac Brigade, in the name of Colonel Blagojevic, and I just wanted to show you that last paragraph, paragraph 8, regarding the 51 UNPROFOR soldiers. Does that relate to what you've previously testified about, about the Dutch -- the Dutch soldiers being moved out?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, those held at the Hotel Fontana.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, 15 July, I want to go to 65 ter 49, just to get a feel on the narrative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have a Main Staff report to the president by General Miletic, standing in for the chief of staff, and just referring you to B/C/S page 3 and English page 3, the Drina Corps section. This gives an update about Zepa and Srebrenica, and the movement of Muslim forces. Can you comment on the accuracy of this information at this time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, in context with the actual operations that were occurring on the ground, on the 15th, the 4th, 6th, and 7th Infantry Battalions were the units of the Zvornik Brigade that absorbed the brunt of the attack from the column at that time carving its way through the rear areas of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And, Mr. Butler, we will -- we're going around the Zvornik area for a while, and we will come back there in the chronology around the 13th, but feel free to comment on it, where appropriate, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But just for everyone's knowledge, that's -- we're not forgetting about Mr. Haynes or Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Any other comments about the accuracy of that information? Is the president being kept up to date?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, it's generally accurate with respect to the military situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter 37.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I believe it's a document that may have been seen here. I don't want to go into a tremendous amount of detail to it -- with it. But it is from the Main Staff, dated 17 July, to the Drina Corps, the Zvornik Brigade and the Bratunac Brigade and the Milici Brigade and the 67th Communication Regiment, in the name of General Mladic. It's entitled: "Integration of operations to crush lagging Muslim forces." Basically, it appears to be divided up into two sections, paragraph 1 and 2, and then the rest of it. Can you -- can you tell us -- just briefly outline what this is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a two-part order. In fact, Part 1 of that order commissions a group of three colonels from the Main Staff to go to the Command of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade as a function of planning and coordinating of combat operations. I believe, particularly before this Trial Chamber, that there has been testimony as to what the actual purpose of these three colonels and their arrival in the Zvornik Brigade was meant to undertake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So let's -- let's go on to the next part, then.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next part is the appointment of Lieutenant-Colonel Keserovic, who is a Main Staff officer working for General Tolimir, as a commander of a grouping of forces. These forces are specified as those forces that are engaged and continuing military operations against the Muslim forces who are still remaining behind and who have been trapped in that pocket bordered by the Konjevic Polje-Milici and Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what about this reference to MUP forces, what are they supposed to do, if anything, with that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the MUP forces that are there would, in fact, fall under the command of Colonel Keserovic when he arrives there as part of that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next document, 65 ter 1214D, B/C/S 65 ter 1214 -- it's the same for both.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is a 17 July intercept between two unknown people - I'm waiting for it to come up - X and Y, and we can read it to ourselves a bit. Then we see, as we get down to it, it says: "Has Keserovic set out already?" X says: "We came across him on our way here." "He hasn't arrived yet." "well, he must have first gone over there to Momir Nikolic." "Uh-huh. Let me tell you, I spoke just a while ago to General Miletic." "Okay. He told me that Keserovic also has to come here to solve these problems." "Yes. However, what I told you this morning, I told the commander, he ordered Salapura and the order will be drafted, or rather, a request to the MUP to bring back all of them, in fact to keep them." "Well, they are leaving. The buses are arriving. They have your order." "I know. Salapura talked to Kovac and got his verbal consent that the shift will arrive in the course of the day."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can go on to page 2 of the B/C/S. The rest of it can be read, but I won't read that. Everyone, if they want, could please read that to themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you relate this to anything?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In the context of the order that we've just discussed, it reflects the fact that individuals on the ground - and again I do not know who the correspondents are - are reporting that the MUP forces that are at that particular location, they either believe or have been directed by MUP officials that their mission is over and that they are to depart the area. There is clearly some confusion between the army, which believes that they're supposed to remain there, and the MUP, which believes they're supposed to be leaving. There's a reference between the army and Mr. Kovac, who is the acting Minister of the Interior, and a discussion that, you know, they have at least talked to him and they have his verbal consent that either those or an additional shift will be arriving during the course of the day, so there may well be MUP replacement forces coming in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: From this intercept, can you get any idea of where Keserovic is actually going?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reference that he must -- "he's supposed to come here," again, I don't know where "here" is. I don't want to speculate, but the fact that he must have "first gone over there to Momir Nikolic" is a reflection that at some juncture he went to the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade prior to his arrival at that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you make any sense out of these next two lines: "I just a while ago to General Miletic -- "I spoke just a while ago to General Miletic." "Okay. He told me that Keserovic also has to come here to solve these issues"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe that's a verbal notification that essentially reflects the written order that we just talked about in the last exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where would -- can you -- and don't speculate. But in that regard, what do you mean by -- where would "here" be?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you know, the most -- based on my broader knowledge of everything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has just said that he doesn't know where it is, "here." So I don't understand how he could know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That was the first "here." There's two "heres" in this intercept. We can go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's turn to 65 ter 91.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This document is entitled: "The Special Police Brigade," the same date, the 17th of July, order by Commander Goran Saric and reference to Ljubomir Borovcanin. Can you just briefly outline what this is and if it has anything to do with what you've just been discussing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe that this is the written manifestation of the conversation that the two correspondents in the prior exhibit were referring to between the discussion of Colonel Salapura and Mr. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is Mr. Borovcanin's responsibility here, just briefly?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, Colonel -- or Mr. Borovcanin at this juncture and some part of the overall MUP forces have already re-deployed from the Bratunac area and are engaged in the zone of the Zvornik Brigade, dealing with issues related to the column. It specifically breaks apart the issue of responsibility, creating two separate battle groups, one that Dusko Jevtic will be the commander on the ground of that second battle group, Borovcanin of the first battle group, but also noting that he is still responsible for command and control of both of the combat groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You said "Dusko Jevtic," this --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Jevric. I want to read the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, take a look. Do you know of a Dusko Jevric?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't. I believe this has to be a reference to Dusko Jevtic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next exhibit, 65 ter 1231A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is an intercept still on 17 July, 1950 hours, A and C. The participants, as we can now see, Krstic and Commander Mladic. We see a reference by General Mladic to Krle: "Can you hear me? He says: "I can hear you, full steam ahead, understood." Mladic says: "Get in touch with Miletic on the secure line, full steam ahead. I didn't accept the Turks' conditions." What do you believe this is a reference to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a reference to the ongoing negotiations back and forth between the Muslim leadership inside the Zepa enclave, the UN -- the UNPROFOR forces there, and General Tolimir, who's representing the interests of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you -- do you have any specific information why Mladic would refer Krstic to Miletic, as opposed to someone else?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Miletic is General Mladic's chief of operations. General Miletic is going along with, you know, General Mladic again telling him, "Get in touch with General Miletic, who is the person who will presumably be able to provide all the operational details and all the other issues that you'll need for the continuation of combat activities." That's not irregular at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madame Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I didn't raise any objection, but this is now too much. Very often, the witness used the word "presumably." I think it's wholly inappropriate. I think he knows or he doesn't, but I don't think he can speculate in such a way. Of course, he can give his opinion, but I don't think he should speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you use or make use of the adverb, presumably, what do you actually mean? Are you speculating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Obviously, I'm not a fact witness. I don't know whether this is a fact or not. When I use the phrase "presumably," I use it, you know, in context with my knowledge of the various JNA and VRS regulations, all of the documents that I've discussed here and that I'm aware of, particularly with issues relating to what the functions of these individuals would have been by their position on -- at various levels of staff. I don't know for a fact that General Miletic would have had, you know, all of the details of the Zepa operation. However, I presume that, given the fact that he is the chief of operations for the Main Staff, that he, more than anyone else at that organisation, would have had the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Let's go to 1237A and C.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's an intercept on the 17th of July at 2055 hours, and there's the name of Trivic, Badem, and Colonel Jankovic. We know what "Badem" is, or you've told us that "Badem" is Bratunac. Colonel Jankovic, who do you believe this is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Jankovic is Colonel Radoslav Jankovic of the Main Staff Intelligence Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And from this, can you conclude where he is on the 17th at this time, or where someone thinks he is, to be more accurate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Badem" is the radio code name for the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. It says: "Well, Jankovic? He says: "Yes." "Listen here. Miletic said ..." "Yes." "... that you should write what you want to do." "Yes." "And send it urgently by code up to Tolimir." Then he says: "I'm in no position, man, to write. I'm calling here, and there is ..." "Listen to what I'm telling you." "All right." "And the commander will decide with Tolimir and send you a reply." "Fine." "Well, all right. Take care, mate." With that in mind, I would like to ask you about the next set of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's 65 ter number 260.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is an 18 July document, basically the next day from that intercept. We see a time of about 1700 hours', and on the typed version we see, "Chief of intelligence organ Momir Nikolic" in both languages. But in the handwritten version, which is page -- on page 4 of the B/C/S, at the bottom, we see those initials which got translated as "RZ." Is this what you had been talking about earlier with the documents we discussed, the previous Radoslav Jankovic document from the 13th?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Madame Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm completely lost. Part of an intercept was read out, with questions to the witness, and now we're going to another document which, personally, I don't see. Could the Prosecution tell us why he's now asking questions about a document which has been shown half an hour ago. I don't understand why the intercept is shown if he has no question to ask from the witness on this intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. Thank you, Madame.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, the intercept makes reference to -- for Jankovic to write down what he wants and send it along to the commander, and Tolimir will decide. Now we have a document that's being sent up to the Main Staff, and I'm getting into, with Mr. Butler, who authored this document and whether it is related or may be related to the previous intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer? Frankly, I would like to answer in the absence of the witness, because this can have some implications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In fact, I had a temptation to stop Mr. McCloskey halfway. But, Mr. Butler, could you kindly leave the courtroom for a short while.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll soon be calling you back. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madame Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, maybe there is a connection, I'm not sure, but the problem, as shown by the Prosecution, he puts in the mouth of the witness that it is connected, without giving him an opportunity to say whether there is a link or not. So in the conversation we've seen, there's also the name of Trivic. Trivic was the commander of a brigade in Zepa and has nothing to do with Bratunac at this moment. Maybe this conversation is only connected to Zepa, I do not know. But if the Prosecutor is asking the question in this way to the witness, then he suggests very clearly that there is a link between the document. And then with the question, we won't get an answer from the witness. It will simply be a confirmation of the argument of the Prosecutor, and this is what I have already said. It is not bearing to the witness. These are the arguments of the Prosecution we've just heard; and, in fact, the witness was for a long time employed by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment further, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not meaning to do that. I'm asking him about documents and asking him if he can relate to them, to each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think, Madame Fauveau, I doubt how right you can be, because if you look at page 63, which is basically the last part of page 63, where the question is: "Is this what you have been talking about earlier with the documents we discussed, the previous Radoslav Jankovic document from the 13th?" So he's not putting anything to the witness. Then later on, if there was any doubt, page 64, line 7 and 8 -- or 5 to 8: "And now we have a document that's being sent up to the Main Staff, and I'm getting into, with Mr. Butler, who ordered this document and whether it is related or may be related to the previous intercept." So he's not put words or suggested a conclusion to the witness, as yet, at least, as I see it. Yes, Madame Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you show him this document first, to my mind, he's just suggesting, by the very fact of showing this document, that there is a link. I would like the witness to explain to us the intercept itself, the conversation, and that he tells us what it is about, this conversation, this intercept. If there is a link, then after that he may then tell us what link there is, what relationship between the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if there is, in Mr. McCloskey's mind, at least, a link between this document and the previous one, why shouldn't he be put in a position to put that question in the first place? I mean, if there is no link, I'm pretty sure that the witness will not hesitate. Yes. Do you wish to comment further or should we bring Mr. Butler back in?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can just, if it's helpful, provide more detail about why I didn't go into that intercept. I don't think you can tell, from this intercept, what he's talking about, except that whatever he's talking about, to write a letter about it. So I didn't ask Mr. Butler to speculate. Sometimes I will ask Mr. Butler, and sometimes I won't, and that's the decision I've got to make in direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, fine. I think we can proceed. Yes, Madame Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is precisely the question, Mr. President. He asks the question about this intercept and what it's about, then he is speculating. If he gives him this document and says it refers to this, then the witness will say, yes, that's possible, but it remains a speculation. It doesn't go any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't want to discuss it much further. In my mind, at least, it is quite clear that he's using the second document to try and give some sense to the first one. I mean, this is basically it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's really -- the Judges will decide -- you will decide if it's related or not. I'm not trying to -- you know, we're just trying to lay it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Even if the witness says that it is related, it stands to us to decide whether we take his word for it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I frankly can't remember what he says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is none of my business, but I anticipated the objection Madame Fauveau was going to make, and she didn't then make it. I don't know why all this can't go in the Prosecution's final brief. Why is this all being adduced through a witness? They're linking documents together through a witness for hour after hour after hour that could go down in writing and have you read it at the end of the case. That's the objection I thought she was going to make, not that it was speculation, but that it is comment by the Prosecution, with the endorsement of a so-called expert witness. But as I say, this is none of my business, and you've ruled on the question, but I hope you'll bear that in mind as we go forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, by putting myself in your shoes, both of you, I think I can quite understand why this is being done, because if it goes in the final brief, then obviously it will have the support of an expert witness. If no question is put, it can well be included in the final brief, but with less weight if it's not supported by anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could I just briefly respond to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, come on. Let's leave it at that, Mr. McCloskey. Let's bring Mr. Butler and continue and get it over and done with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's a very fundamental attack on our theory. I'd like to be able to -- it will take me 20 seconds to explain why this is happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's start counting the seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Imagine a general taking a 3.000-page intelligence report and saying, "Okay, General, you can figure out what the intelligence is," as opposed to a briefing. This is a briefing, and you can take it or leave it, and that's all. That's what we're talking about. With that, we can get Mr. Butler back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The suggestion is that we have the break now because we've been sitting for an hour and a half already. Thank you. Twenty-five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, we were at 65 ter 260, and I think I directed your attention to the handwritten part of that, and you had given us your conclusions. Were you able to look at the original of that -- of that handwritten recently in your analysis on who -- who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I had requested, and it was provided, the original copies of this document, as well as the prior document from Colonel Jankovic. I believe it's dated 13 July, from the ICTY evidence vault.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did you do with the originals, and how did it help or assist in your analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the original handwritten versions, it reinforces my opinion that the author of this particular document, at least the paper draft version of that document, is in fact Colonel Radoslav Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And, Your Honours, I have the originals here, if there's any interest in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Anything unique about the paper in the document that helped this analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a normal white sheet of blank paper or lined paper. The documents, both of whom are attributed to Colonel Jankovic, are on the same type of graph paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go to the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. For the record, I'd like to state that these kind of conclusions made by the witness has no relationship with his expertise. This is a conclusion that can be drawn and should be drawn by an investigator, and the work that he did in comparing these documents and obtaining the originals from the vault is something that is done by investigators. An investigator is not the kind of conclusion that they would be able to come and do before this courtroom. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can briefly refer the Court back to the testimony of Mr. Butler regarding the job of a -- of a military intelligence officer is to look at human intelligence, documents, to determine their authenticity. Its absolutely within his job, both as that and as an analyst, to determine the authenticity and the authorship of the documents that he's analysing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go now, if we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We authorise you to proceed. Of course, we reserve the right of Mr. Bourgon and others to make submissions on this in due course, when appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, that -- let's now go to the English translation of this, and it's on B/C/S page 1 as well. What I'm most interested in the third -- what's marked as the third paragraph, the part about the MSF convoy. Then at the third paragraph down, this question that is asked: "Will you please tell me what stand to take in terms of authorisation for evacuation of the international organisation MSF, in fact, how to deal with so-called local staff. This also applies to the interpreters of the Military Monitors and UNPROFOR. "The RDB passed on to us the opinion that President Karadzic has allegedly abolished all local staff who used to work for UNPROFOR. It is our opinion that they should not be hold." Maybe "should not be held" or "hold." What is your analysis of those -- of that question?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's pretty straightforward, sir. Both, you know, many of them international organisations, did use local nationals, some of them from that particular area, for translation duties. There was an open question as to whether or not, when repatriating back, a number of those members of international organisations are allowing them to leave, whether or not the locally-hired staff should go with them or would they be subject to detention by the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go to the next day, 19 July. We see that that document, as the previous one, 260, was about 5.00 in the evening, 5.00 p.m., 1700.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now let's go to 65 ter 1266D for both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is from the 19th of July, the next day, at about 1432 hours, and it says: "Jankovic's voice at frequency channel 3, and Colonel Djurdjic at another frequency between channels 3 and 4." Participants: Jankovic, Colonel Djurdjic. From your analysis, can you tell who these people are?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Colonel Djurdjic is an officer of the Main Staff who is frequently associated with issues related to the UNPROFOR; and Colonel Jankovic is Colonel Jankovic from the Main Staff intelligence branch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's take a look at this conversation. As we go down it, it says: "Colonel Djurdjic speaking." Then Jankovic says: "I'm listening." Janko?" "Yes." "Is it you?" "Yes, it's me. "We should talk, but I've got to make an effort." "Okay." "Regarding what you were asking." Then Jankovic says: "Yes." "The boss has ordered that they be halted." "Yes." "That is what he wrote." "Yes." "That Kristina, the nurse, can go." "Yes." "Daniel O'Brien." "Yes." "The physician." "Yes." "Can you hear me well?" "Yes." "You here me well?" "I can here you." Then Djurdjic says: "And only women and children can go. Understand?" And on B/C/S, English page 2: "And what about those young men?" Djurdjic says: "Others, no. I don't know." "They might require." And Djurdjic says: "Say again?" Jankovic: "But they will require, but they have government's permission for all of them to go." And then Djurdjic says: "Goddamn it, can we do this through the girl?" "I have to ask her to act as mediator here, and now I'll -- "We can't, we can't. We're having a one-way conversation." And then Jankovic says: "Listen." "Yes." "So, they have permission from the Koljevic Government?" "Yes." "That they can all go. They have a list." "Yes, I know ..." Then they talk about the names of several Muslim men, which I won't go through. Then it goes on: "Yes, they are taking them as local staff, and they have permission from Koljevic." Djurdjic says: "All right. They have the permission, but you know that the procedure you two too took part in. "Great." "Pardon?" "Great. If that's your position, it's good." "The procedure is such, goddamn it, that it should be checked whether those who ... are they able-bodied or older than 60?" Jankovic: "They are able-bodied." "They are?" "Yes." "So that is the procedure, and you saw what you left behind in Bratunac the other day." "Okay." "Am I right?" Jankovic says: "Okay." "All right." "And they, if they agree, let them go in their vehicles and take those women and children." "All right." "And that little orphan, too, some small kid of a year and a half." "Okay." "Understand." "All right." "Is it a deal?" "And they also have two elderly persons." "Say again?" "They have two elderly people with them." "What things?" "No. Two old, two elderly persons, and ... 80, 81 years old." "Those are kids." "No, no, the elderly." "Two elderly, let them go. Let the elderly go." "Okay." "Let the elderly go; and tonight when Tosa areaches, you and him must make sure you consult some more, please." "All right, I will. When is Tosa coming?" "In the early evening." "Okay, I won't." "All right. Talk to you later." "I'll be in touch with him." "Cheers." "Thank you." Okay. Let's go back to the beginning here, and, first of all, can you tell us what they're talking about, generally, in your view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally, they're reviewing to -- they're referring to differing guidance that they've been receiving with respect to what should happen with the local national staff for those international organisations. On one hand, Colonel Djurdjic is saying, "You know what the procedure is, that if they are in fact males of military age, they're to be separated and screened." On the other hand, Colonel Jankovic is saying, "But I have information that they all have permission to include the local staff to leave, and that permission is signed by the president of the" -- not the president, but I mean "the leadership of the Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And when they get down to the last part of it, they're referring to a Tosa arriving and talking with Tosa about this. "Tosa," I'm sorry. Has your analysis revealed to you who you believe Tosa to be?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I understand that that is a nickname commonly used to describe General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next document, 65 ter 3039.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is a document from MSF.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's under seal, I'm told. Excuse me. I don't have it in English, but I'm really not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is dated 19 July 1995, and have you reviewed this in your analysis of the previous intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir; and, in fact, a number of names listed here are mentioned in that previous intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know, did these MSF interpreters and UNMO interpreters make it out okay from the area?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It is my understanding that they, in fact, were not detained and were allowed to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter 3015 now, a 20 July document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We've got "10.30 a.m." written on it. At the bottom, it's from the Drina Corps command, the village of Goranji, the forward command post, 20th of July, to the VRS Main Staff, General Miletic personally, from the commander, General Krstic. He's asking -- or what is he doing, just briefly? You tell us what he's doing.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document, General Krstic is making a request to the Main Staff, General Miletic personally, that orders be given to engage the Military Police Battalion of the 65th Protection Regiment so they can be used in and around Zepa to prevent the looting of materials presumably by VRS forces after they liberate the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, again, I won't go into it in detail, but does this fit the job description for General Miletic, as you've described earlier in a similar document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, General Krstic, as the commander of the Drina Corps, does not have the competence to order a unit that's directly subordinate to the Main Staff. He would have to go through General Miletic and request the employment of that unit. It would be up to the Main Staff to either grant his request, deny it, or modify it in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, the Military Police Battalion, which branch of the Main Staff do they come under?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular context, they are part of the 65th Protection Regiment. They're not an independent military police battalion standing on their own. The 65th Protection Regiment is an operative formation, so it would fall under the operative branch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that particular case, given the unique mission of the 10th Sabotage Detachment with respect to long-range reconnaissance and sabotage operations, their orders are directed by the chief of intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just to clarify, who is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and his subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So would that be more correctly stated "chief of intelligence and security"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, assistant commander for security and intelligence affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to another one, 65 ter 2517, 21 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This one is from General Tolimir, from the Command of the Rogatica Brigade, as we see up in the left corner, VRS Main Staff, to General Miletic personally. It describes the situation in Zepa. Now, this last paragraph, "We believe that..." Where Tolimir is telling Miletic: "We believe that by destroying the refugee columns of Muslim population from the village of Stublici, Radava," a word I can't pronounce, "we would force the Muslims to surrender quickly." That recommendation and the other proposals, why go through Miletic on those?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are operational proposals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The rules in place that we've discussed before regarding laws of international -- related to the International Laws of War in the JNA, is this last recommendation consistent with those rules, the JNA rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If, in the context, they understand that the refugees are in fact not soldiers fleeing, but in fact civilian refugees, they would not be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter 3020.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a 21 July Main Staff report to the president, that we have become familiar with. Again, it's in the name of General Miletic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to B/C/S page 3, English page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There's just a note: "Part of the corps forces are continuing offensive operations, carrying out combat tasks around the Zepa enclave." Is that correct, in your view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. On 21 July, that is still correct. While some forces, particularly from the Zvornik Infantry Brigade were previously withdrawn, there are still Drina Corps forces engaged in these operations, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The number again?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 65 ter number 3020. And if we could have 65 ter 1324A, and B in the B/C/S, it's an intercept, now moving on to 24 July. Page 2 in the B/C/S is the part I want to ask about. Okay. It should be the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There's talk about a generator and hooking up at Konjevic Polje, but then they get into where X says: "And another thing. Since I'm having difficulty reaching Connie up there, tell him this Himzo Mujic." "Mujic?" "Himzo is no longer in prison here. He should be called Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic." "Lieutenant Colonel?" "Popovic. Ask for the switchboard of the Drina Corps and then for extension 91." "Drina Corps. Switchboard, extension 91." "Yes. And he should arrange it personally with him. He's the only one who knows where he went from here and what happened to him. You can do it if you see him somewhere during the day. You pass that on, because I called him on the number he gave me. He's not in his office." Now, this particular Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic, who do you believe that is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the chief of security for the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Himzo Mujic, what would be that person's ethnicity and/or status?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's not a -- given the fact that there's not a father's name in there, it's kind of very difficult to be conclusive. I mean, the name does sound Muslim, but I'm certainly not an expert in that field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. It says: "Himzo is no longer in prison here." What's that a reference to, in your view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be the Drina Corps detention facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what significance, if any, can you draw from this comment that Popovic -- or that he is the only one who knows where he went and from where and what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read anything more into it than what's listed here. It's pretty self-explanatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do -- would a Drina Corps security officer have anything to do with Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we don't need to go through all that again, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next one, 65 ter number 3021.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is another Main Staff report to the president, just a brief reference. This is B/C/S, page 3, and English, page 3. This now says, under, "Situation of the corps: "Operations around Zepa have ceased at the moment as an agreement of surrender was signed with the Muslims." Is this accurately updating the president on that point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, we have communication from General Tolimir, from the Command of the Rogatica Brigade, to the Main Staff, personally to General Gvero or General Miletic. It talks about the agreement on disarmament of Zepa, and I just want to ask you very briefly, Mr. Butler. It's page 1 of the B/C/S, but it's in the second page of the English. There's this comment: "Make a note to them that we don't want them to send a general, considering that we have information that they want to take advantage of his presence according to similar scenario when they took advantage of presence of General Morillon in Srebrenica in 1993." Can you outline what you believe that is a reference to, both from, well, 25 July 1995 and then the Srebrenica 1993 reference?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's fairly explicit that it's a reference to the circumstances in April or May of 1993 where the VRS agreed to a temporary ceasefire to allow General Morillon and UN presence in Srebrenica for the immediate purpose of facilitating the removal of the civilian population that had been trapped in Srebrenica, and, in fact, that that subsequently turned into a -- the creation of a permanent safe area, which they didn't want to see repeated again in 1995 with respect to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go now to 65 ter 190.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're at 25 July. Main Staff Sector for Intelligence and Security. It says, "For the chief, Lieutenant-Colonel Jovica Koranovic. Can you -- if you can, can you give us any information, as we see what they're talking about on -- especially in reference to the bottom: "Later on, General Miletic and I had a conversation with Bulajic, who happened to be at Lugonja's place. He was told that they are not going to vary from the agreement signed between Kusic and Muslim side; although, the Muslim delegation told Bulajic that they did not know who Torlak was." Do you know who the name Bulajic is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he's it's person associated with the RS Exchange Commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go on to the next document, 65 ter number 182.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is from the Main Staff of the VRS, dated 25 July. It's an order by General Mladic, and it talks about: "By means of organised and complete control, prevent the enemy of all uninvited individuals," and it goes on with similar paragraphs. Can you relate this document to any documents that you've previously seen that had to do more with the Srebrenica events?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is - and in fact, in paragraph 4 - a reiteration of the 13 July order which talked about those same basic procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter 3022.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, just to make a quick reference, it's a Main Staff report to the president, 26 July, under Miletic's name again. As we go to B/C/S, page 4, page 4 of the English, we see a notation: "Units engaged in Zepa are securing the evacuation of the Muslim population." Does that reflect a correct update of what's going on, in your view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter 2793.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is from the Rogatica Brigade, again from General Tolimir, to the Main Staff Sector for Intelligence and Security, forward command post for Krstic, and the intelligence organ of the Drina Corps, entitled: "Mine dispositions in Zepa." It says: "During the conversation with Avdo Palic, we found out that the minefields and individual mines were laid at the following locations:" I don't want to get into the minefields, but what, if anything, does this document tell us about Avdo Palic on this date?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reflects that on that date, there was a conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know if he -- if there's any indications whether he was free to meet with other people or anyone else after --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. At this point in time, he was in the custody of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter 3023.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's another Main Staff report to the president. B/C/S, page 4, in the name of General Miletic. I want to go down to the bottom of the first paragraph: "From the Zepa enclave, they tried to break through to the village of Donje Zezeljevo sector, intending to get to the territory of the SRJ." Now, do you have anything -- any other information relating to the movement of Muslims from Zepa to Serbia around this time, 29 July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There are a series of intercepted communications where various members of the VRS are discussing what they're seeing with respect to Muslim soldiers, rather than putting themselves in the custody of the VRS, they were in fact trying to make it over the Drina River and go to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, and we'll get to some of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But on that, let's go to the next document, 29 July 1995, 65 ter 2673. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is again from the Rogatica Brigade, in the morning, 0930 hours, to the Main Staff, Intelligence and Security, Tolimir personally, and the Drina Corps Intelligence and Security, and to General Krstic. And it's from Captain First Class Dragomir Pecanac. Now, Pecanac is a name we've heard before. Do you know if that's related at all to the other person you talked about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Pecanac is the officer on the Main Staff. He works for the Security Department, and he is associated with being responsible, to a large degree, with issues relating to the personal security of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And just looking at paragraph 5 of this document, it's on the second page in the English, but paragraph 5 in the B/C/S. It just makes a reference about unconfirmed reports that Muslims are trying to break through to the right bank of the Drina River, with -- probably with the intention to surrender to forces of the Serbian MUP. Is this the same -- same information we saw in the previous document that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And getting to 31 July, 65 ter 3024, another Main Staff report to the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just a quick reference, again it's from Miletic, and B/C/S page 3; "At 1930 hours we received information that the enemy were building rafts in the Crni Potok sector and escaping to the Drina bank."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: English page 4, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, is this referring to the same topic that the previous two reports of unconfirmed information?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. We're talking about the same general activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now let's go to 65 ter 3036, page 1 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, I think the English translation may be wrong, from which -- and there's question marks. Can you tell, by looking at this, what unit this document is coming from, if you can look at the original?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, which one? Which document are you referring to, tab number? I have a different --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Oh, 70. If you look at the original --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just want to make sure what's matching up with the screen. Okay. It's listed as partially illegible on the English one. But if you look at the B/C/S version, I think you get a clear read that we're in fact talking about the Command of the 1st Podrinje Light Brigade. We're not talking about the Bratunac Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So that would be corrected back to "the Rogatica Brigade"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this is from the chief of organ, Captain Zoran Carkic. Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he is the assistant -- or he is the chief of security for the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. This is listed as "OSVRO." CLLS: "Expansion unknown." Do you have any explanation of what that is, in that top part, or that may be again another --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't. I'm not further with what that "expansion" is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And to General Miletic personally, who do you think that is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the context of this, I believe we're referring to General Miletic of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you have any other VRS officers with that name, besides Zdravko Miletic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, Captain Carkic, I want to refer you to B/C/S page 1. It's page 3 of the English. In speaking to General Miletic, he says: "Another 100 balija are expected in Bajina Basta."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why is that Zdravko?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why "Zdravko"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just got it mixed up. I apologise. I apologise to the general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to the form of the question, because the Prosecution has just said that Captain Zakic, while speaking to General Miletic. First of all, he's not talking to him, and he's not the only addressee and he's not the first addressee, either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. What do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you want me to imply he's speaking to him? I mean, he's communicating to him, and that's what I want to focus on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that what she's saying is not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, that's clear enough. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: "Another 100 balija are expected in Bajina Basta. At the same time, the largest group of balija was registered, around 1.000 men in the general area of Crni Potok. They seem to be attempting to cross over to the right bank." Then there's some more information about other areas, and there's the last comment: "We have information that they register them immediately, and for the time being, they are not inclined to turn them over to us." What do you believe that first reference that I mentioned is, this thousand -- a thousand men?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are individuals who are military-aged men, may very well even be members of the Zepa Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter 1378. That's A in the English, B in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a 1 August intercept between Jevtic from Serbia and Stevo and Ljubisa Beara from the Main Staff of the so-called VRS. Do you know who Jevtic is in this context?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about Stevo?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, say again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about Stevo?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Ljubisa Beara?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know who he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The same question regarding his name, are you aware of any other officers of the VRS with that name, "Beara"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Okay. In page 2, we get on to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In the B/C/S, at the bottom. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't want to go through this entire conversation, but can you just briefly tell us, does this have to do with the subject matter of the documents we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And would the involvement that we see from this intercept of Ljubisa Beara be consistent with his position on the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next one, 389A in English -- 1389A and 1389C.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's an intercept, 10.00, between someone named Mandzuka and General Krstic. Any idea who Mandzuka is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Again, I won't -- I won't get into it. I think we can read this as we see it. It's talking about a thousand of them in Bajina Basta, and Krstic says: "Register all the RS over there so we can use them for exchange. How about more down there?" The person says: "About 2.000, altogether. Beara went over there to Serbia. He'll take care of it." Again, is this the same subject you've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next one, 1392B, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is dated 2 August, and, I'm sorry. I'm going to have to tell you, I will get back to you on the -- I'm going to have to get back to you on the date of the Mandzuka-General Krstic intercept. It's also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's no objection, but was 1389 on the list? Was there a supplemental list including that one, because it doesn't appear on my list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If it's not on the list, I'll skip it. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 1392B. This is 2 August, and we now, if we -- this is a short one between General Krstic and Popovic. 1392 is the B, B/C/S, on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What do you think they're talking about here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this, it's directing General Krstic -- General Krstic is directing General Popovic, as well as a Kosoric; and within the context of where they're located and what they're doing, I take "Kosoric" to be Lieutenant-Colonel Svetozar Kosoric, the chief of intelligence of the Drina Corps, and go over to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next one, 1395B in both languages. It's divided into two pages in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's an intercept on 2 August, between Krstic and Popovic. Who do you believe the "Popovic" and the "Krstic" is here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the same two correspondents, we're talking about General Krstic, the commander of the Drina Corps, and Colonel Popovic, the chief of security of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just, very briefly, does this have to do with the same -- what does this have to do with?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're referring about the same issue. In this particular context, the report that is coming back is that the Serbian MUP is not allowing representatives of the VRS to talk to these individuals, and at present the Serbian MUP is not allowing them to be returned back into the custody of the VRS, so they're staying in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, I have one smaller binder which I will definitely be able to finish tomorrow, and I would hope that during the second period, and, if we're lucky, the first period, if I can get your approval for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey, and that's advanced notice to whoever is going first.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going first, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. We stand adjourned until tomorrow at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 18th day of January, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
